parole.significato: Synonym of dandy or hammock litter, a strong cloth suspended from a pole or set of poles used as an open sedan chair.
parole.testo: From Portuguese andor, from Malayalam, from Sanskrit हिन्दोल (hindola, “swinging cradle, hammock litter, dooly”). Compare dooly from Sanskrit दुल् (dul) via Hindi.

parole.significato: Either of two (parts of) plants often used in combination
parole.testo: Borrowed from Portuguese bétele, from Malayalam വെറ്റില (veṟṟila) or Tamil வெற்றிலை (veṟṟilai).

parole.significato: The dried kernel of the coconut, from which coconut oil is extruded.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Portuguese copra, from Malayalam കൊപ്ര (kopra). Cognate with Tamil கொப்பரை (kopparai), Kuvi କବ୍ରି (kobri), Sanskrit कूर्पस (kūrpasa), Hindi खोपा (khopā).

parole.significato: A jackfruit (Artocarpus heterophyllus, syn. Artocarpus integrifolia).
parole.testo: From Portuguese jaca (“jackfruit”), from Malayalam ചക്ക (cakka).

parole.significato: A tree, Artocarpus heterophyllus, of the Moraceae family, which produces edible fruit.
parole.testo: From jack (“jackfruit”), from Portuguese jaca (“jackfruit”), from Malayalam ചക്ക (cakka) / Tamil சக்கை (cakkai), + fruit.

parole.significato: Any of species Mangifera indica of tropical Asian fruit trees.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Portuguese manga, from Malayalam മാങ്ങ (māṅṅa) / Tamil மாங்காய் (māṅkāy), possibly via Malay mangga, ultimately from Proto-South Dravidian *mām-kāy (“unripe mango”), a compound of *mām (“mango tree”) + *kāy (“unripe fruit”).
